complexity.notes: word_tuple is computed twice per word (once to build the dict, once to append); a collections.defaultdict(list) or dict.setdefault would avoid the redundant work and be cleaner. The annotation 'tuple(int)' is a runtime call, not a type hint — it should be 'tuple[int, ...]'. Worst case is O(n^2) because adversarial hash collisions degrade dict operations to O(n) each.
complexity.summary: Each word is mapped to a 26-element letter-count tuple used as a dict key, and words are grouped by identical signatures. Since word length is bounded by a small constant, each signature is computed in O(1), giving linear average time overall.
